name: Banded Mail
description: Laminar armor with overlapping metal strips. Includes vambraces, greaves, and/or armored sleeves. Lighter than other armors in its category but may be more difficult to maintain.

name: Brigandine
description: Cloth or leather garment lined with small steel plates, riveted to the fabric. Typically worn over padded undergarment. AC 14 and weight 20 lbs if worn without undergarment.

name: Chain Mail
description: Interwoven metal rings worn over padded undergarment. Very flexible and durable. AC 14 and weight 30 lbs if worn without undergarment.

name: Field Plate Mail
description: Solid plate armor pieces with sliding parts, hinges, and straps. Small chain mail pieces cover joints. Must be custom fitted. AC 17 and weight 60 lbs if worn without undergarment.

name: Full Plate Mail
description: Superior design of field plate armor. Covers wearer more fully, generally without chain mail. Deflects weapon strikes from vulnerable joints. -1 penalty to attack rolls due to limited mobility. Requires assistance to put on, takes at least 1 turn to don.

name: Hide
description: Made from cured beast hide sewn to clothing. Common in remote or barbaric areas. Hot and itchy, but offers protection similar to leather.

name: Leather
description: Made of hardened and/or layered leather pieces sewn to a cloth undergarment. Offers flexibility and moderate protection.

name: No Armor
description: Unarmored.

name: Padded or Quilted
description: Created from layers of cloth. Often ceremonial, offers minimal protection. Good insulation for winter, but requires frequent laundering. Used as undergarment for metal armors.

name: Plate Mail
description: Large metal plates covering torso, arms, and legs, attached to chain mail. Worn over padded undergarment. AC 16 and weight 40 lbs if worn without undergarment.

name: Ring Mail
description: Steel rings sewn directly to a soft, supple leather undergarment. Offers great flexibility and decent protection.

name: Scale Mail
description: Metal scales woven to an undergarment. Offers flexibility and moderate protection. Includes Lamellar armor.

name: Splint Mail
description: Chain mail with small strips of thick metal interwoven. Offers better protection than regular chain mail but heavier and less flexible.

name: Studded Leather
description: Leather armor with metal studs or small plates riveted to it. Offers added protection at slight cost of mobility.

name: Ale, common
description: Ales are brewed or fermented from grains that use yeast to make the alcohol content. These are generally not as potent as spirits and are usually produced at monasteries. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

description: Ales are brewed or fermented from grains that use yeast to make the alcohol content. These are generally not as potent as spirits and are usually produced at monasteries. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

description: Ales are brewed or fermented from grains that use yeast to make the alcohol content. These are generally not as potent as spirits and are usually produced at monasteries. name: Applejack
description: Applejack is a strong and cheap brandy produced from apples.

name: Cider, common
description: Cider is generally made from non-citrus fermented fruit juices like apples, pears, peaches, and many different berries. Citruses like oranges, limes, and lemons have acids that kill the yeast used to ferment the juice.

name: Mead, common
description: Mead is made with honey diluted with water or apple juice, and fermented with wine yeast. It is a potent drink popular in northern climates. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

name: Mead, common
description: Mead is made with honey diluted with water or apple juice, and fermented with wine yeast. It is a potent drink popular in northern climates. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

name: Small Beer
description: Small Beer is a low-alcohol beer. This lightly-fermented brew is almost a liquid snack, and keeps clean better than water. Suitable for adventuring, though it may turn ‘dank’ if left in a wineskin for too long. Beers are brewed or fermented from grains that use yeast to make the alcohol content. These are generally not as potent as spirits and are usually produced at monasteries.

name: Small Beer
description: Beers are brewed or fermented from grains that use yeast to make the alcohol content. These are generally not as potent as spirits and are usually produced at monasteries. Small Beer is a low-alcohol beer. This lightly-fermented brew is almost a liquid snack, and keeps clean better than water. Suitable for adventuring, though it may turn ‘dank’ if left in a wineskin for too long.

name: Spirits, common
description: Spirits are fermented alcohols that are boiled again to remove the water and increase the alcohol content. The type of spirit is dependent on the grain, grape, fruit, or berry used as a base. These are generally made by a local farmer. Quality depends on the experience of the person making the spirit and the quality of the crop. Spirits are generally mixed or ‘cut’ with water to make the bottle last longer. Common spirits are half water and half alcohol and have an acceptable taste.

description: Spirits are fermented alcohols that are boiled again to remove the water and increase the alcohol content. Exceptional spirits are not cut and usually are not mixed with any other liquids. The prices given are minimum.

name: Wine, common
description: Wine is made from fermented grape juices (or sometimes other berries or fruits). The type of grapes determine the color and flavor of the wine. Monasteries often produce the best wines. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

description: Wine is made from fermented grape juices (or sometimes other berries or fruits). The type of grapes determine the color and flavor of the wine. Monasteries often produce the best wines. Common drinks are the cheapest, and are a passable- quality offering.

name: Apron, Canvas
description: An Apron is a loose piece of material that has a loop that goes over the wearer's head with two long strings at the sides that are either tied in the back or are wrapped around the waist and tied at the front.Canvas is used for covering where the user isn't exposed to heat very often. Tavern keeps, cooks, butchers, potters, and artists are the most common users.

name: Apron, Leather
description: An Apron is a loose piece of material that has a loop that goes over the wearer's head with two long strings at the sides that are either tied in the back or are wrapped around the waist and tied at the front. Leather is used where there is a chance of something that could go through a canvas apron for such professions as smithies (any), coopers (barrel makers), armorers, weapon makers, and masons.

name: Baldric, Belt Sash
description: A Baldric or Belt Sash is a belt worn across the torso with attachment for a scabbard. Typically this rests the weapon at the hip, but a scabbard could easily be attached to the back of the baldric for an over-the-shoulder draw. Small pouches or weapon scabbards may be attached to a baldric strap. This includes Bandoleers.

name: Belt
description: A Belt is a strip of leather worn around the waist to help hold up a person's trousers or pants. A scabbard could also be hung from it.

name: Belt Hook or Ring
description: A Hook or Ring is a weapon attachment for a belt or strap, to hold an axe, hammer, or mace. It is effectively a scabbard for a hafted weapon.

name: Belt, Money Belt
description: A Money belt is a broad leather belt including one or two slim, hidden pouches for hiding coins or other small goods It has a maximum capacity of about 50 coins.

name: Belt, Weapon Belt
description: A Weapon belt is a large, heavy belt designed to distribute the weight of a weapon across the hips, while holding it in position for easy retrieval.

name: Blouse, Linen
description: A Blouse is a loose-fitting shirt buttoned down the front. This is the upper clothing worn by many commoners and craftspeople.

name: Boots, High
description: Boots are a kind of shoe with a top that covers the ankle or higher. High boots go up to the wearer's knee, but the upper portion is loose. Since boots have a harder sole that the leather is attached to, they make a lot of noise on tile floors. A Thief trying to Move Silently while wearing them has a 10% penalty.

name: Boots, Low
description: Boots are a kind of shoe with a top that covers the ankle or higher. Low boots come up just over the wearer's ankles. Since boots have a harder sole that the leather is attached to, they make a lot of noise on tile floors. A Thief trying to Move Silently while wearing them has a 10% penalty.

name: Boots, Riding
description: Boots are a kind of shoe with a top that covers the ankle or higher. Riding boots are knee-high with a tight-fitting upper portion. Since boots have a harder sole that the leather is attached to, they make a lot of noise on tile floors. A Thief trying to Move Silently while wearing them has a 10% penalty.

name: Boots,Swash-topped
description: Boots are a kind of shoe with a top that covers the ankle or higher. Swash-topped boots go up to the wearer's knee, but the upper portion is loose and have a section that is folded over from the top. Since boots have a harder sole that the leather is attached to, they make a lot of noise on tile floors. A Thief trying to Move Silently while wearing them has a 10% penalty.

name: Bracers
description: Bracers are strips of leather that wrap around the lower arm between the elbow and wrist, providing protection to archers from the bowstring striking the inside of the lower arm while firing a bow.

name: Breeches
description: Breeches are short pants ending just below the knee. A Doublet is a long-sleeved jacket that is fitted down to the waist.

name: Bustle
description: A Bustle is similar to a skirt and actually fits under a skirt to give it a fuller shape.

name: Cap
description: A Cap is a soft fabric headcover with no real shape, usually without a brim. Woolen Caps are the traditional beanie cap.

name: Cap, Woolen
description: A Cap is a soft fabric headcover with no real shape, usually without a brim. Woolen Caps are the traditional beanie cap.

name: Cape, Full
description: A Full Cape is a section of cloth that extends from the neck to thefloor, and is attached at the neck by a brooch or clasp. A hood can be attached to cover the wearer's head during inclement weather or to hide one's appearance.

name: Cape, Half
description: A Half Cape is a section of cloth that extends from the neck to the waist, and is attached at the neck by a brooch or clasp. A hood can be attached to cover the wearer's head during inclement weather or to hide one's appearance.

name: Cloak, Adventurers
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. Adventurer's Cloaks are full-length with a long hood that can be used to stash valuables.

name: Cloak, Fur
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. Fur Cloaks are full length hooded cloaks made of tanned furs.

name: Cloak, Fur trimmed
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. Fur Trimmed Cloaks are plain cloaks, with strips of fur trimming the edges. They are also usually more decorated and colorful.

name: Cloak, Leather
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. Leather Cloaks are full length hooded cloaks made of leather instead of wool.

name: Cloak, Plain
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. A Plain Cloak can be either short or full-length, and has a closer-fitting hood.

name: Cloak, Traveling
description: A Cloak is similar to a cape, but includes a hood to cover the wearer's head. Traveling Cloaks are half-length and have a slit to allow the cloak to be draped over either side of a rider's horse.

name: Coat, Fur
description: Fur Coats are full length coats, well tanned with the fur on the outside.

name: Coat, Leather
description: Leather Coats are the same cut, but made of soft leather.

name: Coat, Long
description: A Coat, Long is a long sleeved coat that falls to about the mid-shins, and is made of wool, felt, serge or canvas.

name: Corset
description: A Corset is a support garment commonly worn to hold and train the torso into a desired shape. It is usually either boned cloth or leather.

name: Foot wraps
description: Foot wraps are long pieces of cloth that are wrapped around the feet to prevent cuts or scrapes while walking in the cold or over rough ground, and are usually worn by peasants. Thieves could use these with a bonus of 10% when Moving Silently.

name: Girdle
description: A Girdle is a strip of cloth that is wrapped and tied around a person's midsection and provides some relief to back pain from riding in a saddle over long distances. A Gorget is a band of cloth worn around the neck without the knot showing.

name: Gloves
description: Gloves are hand coverings with each finger separated. Use a -2 modifier to Dexterity if a character is wearing gloves and tries to do an action requiring a DEX roll.

name: Gloves, Fur Lined
description: Gloves are hand coverings with each finger separated. Use a -2 modifier to Dexterity if a character is wearing gloves and tries to do an action requiring a DEX roll.

name: Hat, Cloth
description: A Hat is a shaped head covering with a brim. A Headband is a leather band to keep the wearer's hair out of their eyes.

name: Hat, Fur
description: A Hat is a shaped head covering with a brim. A Headband is a leather band to keep the wearer's hair out of their eyes.

name: Hat, Straw
description: A Hat is a shaped head covering with a brim. A Headband is a leather band to keep the wearer's hair out of their eyes.

name: Headband
description: A Headband, Tooled is a finely tooled and decorated version of the headband.

name: Headband, Tooled
description: A Headband, Tooled is a finely tooled and decorated version of the headband.

name: Hood or Cowl, Wool or Linen
description: A Hood is a detachable piece of clothing to wear with a cape that covers the wearers head. A Cowl is a hood with a very short cape piece that covers the shoulders.
oneLiner: Hood or Cowl, Wool or Linen, 0.2gp, 1lb

name: Hose
description: A Hose is a tight-fitting footed legging that comes up to the crotch.

name: Hose Supporter/Garter
description: Hose Supporters comes in two types; a garter that fits around the leg, and a garter belt that fits around the body and has several thongs hanging down that attach to the top of the hose.

name: Jacket
description: A Jacket is a long-sleeved covering for a shirt. It can either be pulled over the head or buttoned.

name: Jacket, Leather
description: A Jacket is a long-sleeved covering for a shirt. It can either be pulled over the head or buttoned.

name: Jerkin, Leather
description: A Jerkin is a sleeveless jacket that may be worn over a doublet.

name: Jerkin, Wool or Linen
description: A Jerkin is a sleeveless jacket that may be worn over a doublet.

name: Leggings
description: Leggings are tight cloth or leather pants that use a heavier material than hose.

name: Loincloth
description: A Loincloth is usually made from leather or animal skins and just covers the wearer's private parts. It is mostly used by barbarians, ogres, and trolls.

name: Mittens
description: Mittens are hand coverings where the fingers are all together. Use a -4 modifier to Dexterity if a character is wearing mittens and attempts an action involving that ability score.

name: Robe, Common
description: A Robe is a garment that extends to the floor, and is usually worn by royalty, Magic-Users, and Clerics. The Common version is not adorned and is used for daily wear.

name: Robe, Embroidered
description: A Robe is a garment that extends to the floor, and is usually worn by royalty, Magic-Users, and Clerics. An Embroidered robe is for formal occasions.

name: Robe, Lounging
description: A Robe is a garment that extends to the floor, and is usually worn by royalty, Magic-Users, and Clerics. The Lounging version isn't made for heavy use, and is usually of a light material.

name: Sandals
description: Sandals are hard-soled footwear with leather straps to fasten them.

name: Sash
description: A Sash is a cloth or silk version of a belt that is usually used to hold a robe, surcoat, or toga tightly to the body. A Scabbard covers the blade of a knife or sword, and may be readily attached to a belt or harness to safely carry the weapon.

name: Scarf
description: A Scarf is a square of cloth that is folded on the diagonal and then tied under the wearer's chin.

name: Shoes
description: Shoes are footwear that doesn't go above the user's ankles. They have a hard sole and can be noisy on tiled floors.

name: Shoes, Moccasins
description: Moccasins have a soft sole which allow a Thief a 5% better chance of Moving Silently.

name: Skirt or Kilt
description: A Skirt or Kilt is a form of garment that covers the wearers mid-section and extends at least to the knees. Skirts are usually floor length. Kilts are a kind of skirt specifically worn by men. The pattern of the plaid on a kilt is an indication of the tribe that a man is from.

name: Skirt or Kilt, Leather
description: A Skirt or Kilt is a form of garment that covers the wearers mid-section and extends at least to the knees. Skirts are usually floor length.

name: Slippers
description: Slippers are like moccasins without a back portion, but there is a chance that they could fall off while walking or running.

name: Snowshoes
description: Snowshoes are a loop of wood with a mesh of leather thongs across it. It is tied onto a pair of shoes to allow the wearer to walk on top of snow, but at 1/3 of their movement rate.

name: Surcoat
description: A Surcoat is a section of cloth with a hole cut out that fits over the wearer's head. It is generally worn by knights as a cover over armor and may have the knight's heraldry embroidered upon it, though an embroidered version will cost twice as much.

name: Suspenders / Braces
description: Suspenders/Braces are strips of cloth that connect to trousers or pants and go over the shoulders to hold the trousers/pants up.

name: Tabards
description: A Tabard is similar to a Surcoat, but is meant for royal courts with even fancier embroidery that is related to the king's heraldry.

name: Toga
description: A Toga is a lightweight length of material that is wrapped around the body and is draped over one shoulder.

name: Trousers or Trews
description: Trousers or Trews are garments with two legs and covering the waist. Trousers are looser-fitting than leggings. Trews are tighter fitting than trousers but still looser than leggings and are typically plaid like kilts. The plaid pattern is again an indication of the tribe to which the wearer belongs.

name: Trousers or Trews, Leather
description: Trousers or Trews are garments with two legs and covering the waist.

name: Tunic
description: A Tunic is a loose garment draped over the shoulders and going at least to the wearer's knees if not the floor. A Shirt or Chemise is a loose-fitting garment similar to a blouse that is pulled over the head.

name: Turban
description: A Turban is a length of cloth that is wrapped around the wearer's head, usually in arid or desert settings. During dust storms, a portion of the turban can be brought down over the wearer's eyes and mouth to prevent sand from getting in the wearer's face.

name: Veil, Silk
description: A Veil is a short piece of cloth that is hung over the wearer's face for religious ceremonies or to cover a disfigurement. A Thief may want to wear one as part of a disguise.

name: Vest, Cloth w/Pockets
description: Vests are sleeveless garments worn over a shirt.

name: Vest, Fur / Leather
description: Vests are sleeveless garments worn over a shirt.

name: Wig
description: A Wig is a close-fitting cloth with either human or animal hair that is styled, and many times worn by members of government or law. A Thief may try to style one as part of a disguise.

name: Backpack, Adventurer's
description: Volume held: 3 cu ft. Weight held: 40 pounds. Backpacks are assumed to be of heavy canvas or leather.

name: Backpack, Halfling
description: Volume held: 1 1/2 cu ft. Weight held: 30 pounds. Backpacks are assumed to be of heavy canvas or leather.

name: Backpack, Knapsack
description: Volume held: 2 cu ft. Weight held: 25 pounds. A Knapsack is a small cloth backpack, basically a sack with shoulder straps.

name: Backpack, Wicker
description: Volume held: 2 cu ft. Weight held: 15 pounds. A Wicker backpack is essentially an inexpensive and not very sturdy basket with shoulder straps.

name: Bag, Cloth
description: Volume held: 1/4 cu ft. Weight held: 5 pounds.

name: Bag, Cloth, tiny
description: Volume and weight held not specified.

name: Beltpouch
description: Volume held: 1/4 cu ft. Weight held: 2 pounds.

name: Large Pouch or Purse
description: Volume held: 1/2 cu ft. Weight held: 5 pounds. Pouches are small bags or pockets attached to a belt, tucked in a pocket, or hung from a cord.

name: Pack Vest
description: Volume held: 2 cu ft. Weight held: 15 pounds. A Packvest is a leather vest set with multiple pouches and pockets on the front, sides, and inside, and a thin pouch set into the back. While it does not have the capacity of a full backpack, it is less cumbersome, fitting closer to the body and putting various tools and items within easy reach.

name: Sack, Large
description: Volume held: 4 cu ft. Weight held: 40 pounds. Sacks are made from burlap (a rough hemp fiber material), cotton, or leather, and are basically a tube- shaped.  Burlap is used mostly for large grains and small vegetables like corn (maize), beans, peppers, and hard- rind fruits like apples, oranges, and other citrus. Cotton material is used for small grains like rice, oats, or barley and for dry powdery material like flour and sugar.

name: Sack, Large Leather
description: Volume held: 4 cu ft. Weight held: 60 pounds. Leather will provide a waterproof protection for dry powdery material and anything else stored in a sack.

name: Sack, Small
description: Volume held: 2 cu ft. Weight held: 20 pounds. Sacks are made from burlap (a rough hemp fiber material), cotton, or leather, and are basically a tube- shaped.  Burlap is used mostly for large grains and small vegetables like corn (maize), beans, peppers, and hard- rind fruits like apples, oranges, and other citrus. Cotton material is used for small grains like rice, oats, or barley and for dry powdery material like flour and sugar.

name: Sack, Small Leather
description: Volume held: 2 cu ft. Weight held: 30 pounds. Leather will provide a waterproof protection for dry powdery material and anything else stored in a sack.

name: Saddle Bags, Large
description: Volume held: 1 cu ft. Weight held: 10 pounds. Saddle bags are leather bags designed to fit over the back of a riding saddle and provide some storage on a ridden animal. The bags are tied to the saddle to prevent them from falling off. A person can throw them over their shoulder to make sure any valuables that are in the saddlebags are not stolen while the rider is off their mount. The size is in relation to the size of the riding animal.

name: Saddle Bags, Small
description: Volume held: 1/2 cu ft. Weight held: 5 pounds. Saddle bags are leather bags designed to fit over the back of a riding saddle and provide some storage on a ridden animal. The bags are tied to the saddle to prevent them from falling off. A person can throw them over their shoulder to make sure any valuables that are in the saddlebags are not stolen while the rider is off their mount. The size is in relation to the size of the riding animal.

name: Satchel / Haversack
description: Volume held: 1 cu ft. Weight held: 10 pounds. A Satchel or Haversack is a cloth or canvas shoulder- slung bag, designed to rest on the hip or slung behind. Generally a satchel is easier to access than a backpack, but displaces most hip weapons (anything larger than a dagger or handaxe). It is not uncommon to attach a Haversack to a Baldric, giving it a sturdier and more useful strap. These bags are large enough to hold a fair- sized book (such as a spellbook), making them popular among Magic-Users. These bags may be built with internal compartments. The Oilskin Satchel is made from waterproofed leather, providing better protection to its contents.

name: Satchel, Oilskin
description: Water resistant. Volume held: 1 cu ft. Weight held: 15 pounds. A Satchel or Haversack is a cloth or canvas shoulder- slung bag, designed to rest on the hip or slung behind. Generally a satchel is easier to access than a backpack, but displaces most hip weapons (anything larger than a dagger or handaxe). It is not uncommon to attach a Haversack to a Baldric, giving it a sturdier and more useful strap. These bags are large enough to hold a fair- sized book (such as a spellbook), making them popular among Magic-Users. These bags may be built with internal compartments. The Oilskin Satchel is made from waterproofed leather, providing better protection to its contents.

name: Candles
description: 12 candles. A Candle will shed light over a 5 foot radius, with dim light extending a further 5 feet. A normal candle will burn about 3 turns per inch of height.

name: Chalk
description: Small bag of chalk pieces. Chalk is useful for 'blazing a trail' through a dungeon or ruin to ensure that the adventurers can find their way back out again.

name: Charcoal sticks
description: Sticks of charcoal for writing or drawing. Charcoal consists of pieces of carbonized wood, which can be used like chalk (making black markings), or may be added to tinder.

name: Coal Keeper
description: A small, lined ceramic pot designed to hold and keep a small coal or ember lit for several hours. While this will resist moisture and wind, immersion will extinguish the coal immediately.

name: Cord/Strap
description: Per 3 feet of cord or strap. A short length of thin rope, leather, or a short belt for tying something to an arm, leg, or other accessories. This can secure a scabbard to an arm or leg, or attach a pouch to a baldric, or the strap of a backpack.

name: Fine Paper or Vellum
description: Per sheet of fine paper or vellum. High quality paper and vellum is not necessarily more durable, but will take ink better, and is required for magic writing (both books and scrolls).

name: Flask, Silver
description: A silver flask for holding liquids. Flasks are metal containers with stoppers that hold between 8 and 12 oz of liquid.

name: Flask, Steel
description: A steel flask for holding liquids. Flasks are metal containers with stoppers that hold between 8 and 12 oz of liquid.

name: Iron Spikes
description: 12 iron spikes. Iron Spikes are useful for spiking doors closed (or spiking them open) and may be used as crude pitons in appropriate situations.

name: Jar or Bottle, Ceramic
description: A ceramic container for liquids or small items. Jars include lids or stoppers and have a volume of 8-16 oz (double or halve price for larger/smaller volumes). They are good for wet or dry materials, but prone to breakage.

name: Jar or Bottle, Glass
description: A glass container for liquids or small items. Jars include lids or stoppers and have a volume of 8-16 oz (double or halve price for larger/smaller volumes). They are good for wet or dry materials, but prone to breakage.

name: Ladder, Rope
description: 25 feet of rope ladder. A Rope Ladder is a regularly knotted rope, or two lengths of rope, strung with rungs, with a single line at top for a hook. It typically has an 850 lb capacity.

name: Lantern, Bullseye
description: A lantern with a focused beam of light. A Lantern (Bulls-eye) is similar to a hooded lantern, only it is closed on all but one lensed side. This lamp projects light up to 30 feet, and 30 feet at its widest, and includes a shutter.

name: Lantern, Hooded
description: A lantern with an adjustable hood. A Hooded Lantern has a shutter mechanism to close off the light and prevent it from being seen.

name: Lens, small
description: A small magnifying lens. A Lens enlarges the image of an object; a bare lens is smaller and is limited to 2-3x magnification. Both can be used to attempt to start fires using strong sunlight.

name: Magnifying glass
description: A tool for viewing small objects or text. A Magnifying Glass consists of a large lens held in a frame with a handle. It is of higher quality with a minimum of 5x magnification. Can be used to attempt to start fires using strong sunlight.

name: Mirror, small metal
description: A small metal mirror. A Mirror is useful in a dungeon environment for many reasons. For instance, it is the only way to look at a medusa without being turned to stone. Mirrors are also useful for looking around corners, and can be used outdoors to send signals using reflected sunlight.

name: Mirror, small silver
description: A small silver mirror. A Mirror is useful in a dungeon environment for many reasons. For instance, it is the only way to look at a medusa without being turned to stone. Mirrors are also useful for looking around corners, and can be used outdoors to send signals using reflected sunlight.

name: Paper or Parchment
description: Per sheet of paper or parchment. Paper of decent quality, refined papyrus, cotton, cloth, or wood pulp, or parchment – depending on the setting & availability.

name: Rope, Hemp
description: Per 50 feet of hemp rope. Hemp Rope is ½ inch in diameter and has a breaking strength of 1,600 pounds. A safe working load for a rope is normally one-quarter of the breaking strength. One or more knots in a rope cut the breaking strength in half.

name: Rope, Silk
description: Per 50 feet of silk rope. Silk Rope is about 3/8 inch in diameter and has a breaking strength of 1,600 pounds, although it weighs considerably less than hemp rope. The notes regarding rope strength given for hemp rope apply here also.

name: String/Twine
description: 100 feet of string or twine. String / Twine holds up to 30 lb.

name: Wax, beeswax
description: A block of beeswax. Wax, beeswax is a softer wax, useful for making impressions, hasty patches, stuffing in ears, etc.

name: Meal, Banquet (per person)
description: Includes multiple courses and a variety of offerings. The price includes personnel for service, but does not cover entertainment.

name: Meal, Common
description: Includes good bread & cheese, hearty stew, roast fowl or small game, cured meats, fruits and vegetables in season.

name: Meal, Merchant's (Good quality)
description: Includes roast meats, cheeses, light breads, fruits and vegetables, soups, and more 'prepared' dishes. Preserved fruits are offered as well.

name: Meal, Poor
description: Includes dark or rough bread, butter or hard cheese, porridge, broth soups or simple stew, and 'Chef's specials'.

name: Meal, Rich
description: Offers a few courses of different foods like those listed in the Merchant listing, of exceptional quality.

name: Adventurer Pack 2
description: Glass bottle; Iron Spikes, 12; Pole, 10 ft wooden; Map or scroll case; Mirror, small metal. Ready for anything.

name: Bag Option 1
description: Backpack (normal or Halfling), Weapon Belt, Large Pouch. Capacity: 45 lb (35 lb for Halflings.

name: Bag Option 2
description: Oilskin Satchel, Baldric, Weapon Belt, Large Pouch, Belt Pouch(2). Capacity: 24 lb.

name: Camp Cook Kit
description: Iron pan, iron pot, Fire grate, mess kit, common spices, dried meat (2lb), standard rations (5 days), teapot.

name: Cleric Pack
description: Bandages (10), Holy symbol, holy water (1), parchment (2), ink and quill, 1 week rations, tinderbox, waterskin. Protect and spread the faith.

name: Dungeon Mapper
description: 10 sheets paper, ink, quill & quill knife, writing board, bag of chalk pieces.

name: Fighter Pack
description: Bandages (5), Oil, cooking pot, 1 week rations, 3 large sacks, tinderbox, torches (6), waterskin, whetstone. Camp and battle basics.

name: Magic-User Pack
description: Writing ink and quill, parchment (5), scroll case(2), spellbook*, hand mirror, 1 week rations, Torches (6), Tinderbox, glass vial. Scholar & Spellcaster. *The spell book is free for beginning Magic-Users; weight figure assumes a travel spellbook (½ lb).

name: Thief Pack
description: Candles (12), crowbar, grappling hook, mallet, iron spikes (12), 1 wk rations, large sack, small lens, Thieves' tools, tinderbox, waterskin, whetstone. Tools of the trade.

name: Carcass, Game Animal
oneLiner: Carcass, Game Animal, 1.0 per HDgp, varieslb

name: Grain and stabling for horse (daily)
description: Usually done at a Livery or Stable. Liveries offer comprehensive services including farrier service and tack. Stables associated with inns may require owners to feed their own horses.

name: Inn lodging, Common (per day)
description: Includes a room and a day's meals. Room shared with another person, common meals provided. Rooms cleaned about 3 times a week.

name: Inn lodging, Common (per week)
description: Includes a room and a week's meals. Room shared with another person, common meals provided. Rooms cleaned about 3 times a week.

name: Inn lodging, Poor (per day)
description: Includes a room and a day's meals. Lackluster meals, room and bed shared with 3 others. Room cleaned about once a week.

name: Inn lodging, Poor (per week)
description: Includes a room and a week's meals. Lackluster meals, room and bed shared with 3 others. Room cleaned about once a week.

name: Inn lodging, Private Room (per day)
description: Includes a room and a day's meals. Room cleaned daily, good-quality meals, and no sharing of room or bed.

name: Inn lodging, Private Room (per week)
description: Includes a room and a week's meals. Room cleaned daily, good-quality meals, and no sharing of room or bed.

name: Separate latrine for rooms (per month)
description: A separate room or shed for a latrine, available for more expensive lodgings. Common and poor accommodations typically have shared latrines.

name: Bell, small
description: A small bell.

name: Bellows
description: A Bellows is a fire tending tool that is about a foot long with a leather air bag between two wooden handles. When the handles are squeezed together, air will blow out the nozzle of the air bag, increasing the heat of a fire as well as clearing dust or ash.

name: Block and tackle
description: A Block and tackle is a system of two or more pulleys with a rope threaded between them to reduce the weight of loads that are being lifted. The effective weight is reduced by ¼ with one pulley (lifting at load up 50 feet with 100 feet of rope), ½ with two pulleys (with 200 feet of rope), and by with three pulleys (with 400 feet of rope).⅔

name: Bucket
description: Holds up to 5 gallons. Weight when full: 15 pounds.

name: Canvas
description: Per square yard.

name: Chain, Heavy
description: Per foot of heavy chain.

name: Chain, Light
description: Per foot of light chain.

name: Chisel
description: A tool for carving or cutting hard materials.

name: Crowbar
description: A Crowbar a bar of iron that curves at one end in a kind of hook shape. The end itself is flattened with a narrow split on the tip to help pull nails out of a board. The other end is flattened without a split to help pry one piece of wood from another or force open a jammed or locked door, or heavy objects such as a stone coffin lid. In game terms, add one to the die roll range when forcing a door with this tool. For example, a character with 16 Strength would open doors on 1-3 on 1d6; with a crowbar, the range becomes 1-4 on 1d6.

name: Fishing net
description: 10 feet square.

name: Grease Pot
description: Grease is a thick, slippery lubricant made from made from animal fat, or oil from the ground. It is sold in a tin or jar, and is useful for cooking or lubrication. Not all forms are flammable or edible.

name: Hammer or Mallet
description: A tool for striking or pounding.

name: Hand Drill
description: A tool for making holes.

name: Hourglass
description: Measures one hour.

name: Ladder
description: 10 feet long.

name: Marbles, Bag
description: A bag of marbles.

name: Needle, sewing
description: A small needle for sewing.

name: Paint, per gallon
description: Cost ranges from 1-2 gp per gallon.

name: Paint, small pot
description: A small pot of paint.

name: Pick Axe, Mining
description: A Pick Axe is a 'T' shaped tool with a wooden handle, and a combination metal hammer and pick at the end. It is designed for breaking up stones and soil or prying things open. It is also used for prospecting or ice climbing. It deals 1d3 points of damage if used as a weapon.

name: Pliers
description: A hand tool used to hold objects firmly.

name: Pole, 10 ft Collapsing
description: Collapsing Pole is a handy invention consisting of ten 1- foot wood sections, and two metal end caps. Each piece is threaded so that the pieces can be combined to make a pole of any needed length. Collapsing poles from the same maker may be combined for longer reach.

name: Pole, 10 ft wooden
description: A standard 10-foot wooden pole.

name: Scissors
description: A cutting instrument.

name: Arrow, Longbow
description: An arrow composed of an arrowhead, shaft, and flights.

name: Arrow, Shortbow
description: An arrow composed of an arrowhead, shaft, and flights.

name: Battle Axe
description: A standard axe for combat

name: Blowgun
description: A long, hollow tube that uses lung power to fire small darts.

name: Boar Spear
description: A spear with a crossbar to prevent impaled opponents from reaching the wielder.

name: Bola
description: A weapon with weights on the ends of a cord, good for entangling.

name: Bullet Crossbow
description: A crossbow that fires a bullet.

name: Cestus/Spiked Gauntlet
description: A gauntlet with spikes on it.

name: Chain
description: A length of chain that can be used as a weapon.

name: Club/Cudgel/Walking Staff
description: A simple bludgeoning weapon.

name: Crowbar
description: A tool that can be used as an improvised weapon.

name: Dagger
description: A short, sharp blade, good for thrusting.

name: Dart / Throwing Blade
description: A small, sharp projectile.
oneLiner: Dart / Throwing Blade, 1gp, Dmg 1d3, * to ½lb

name: Defending Dagger
description: A dagger with features to help catch or defend against other blades

name: Flail
description: A weapon with a weighted head attached to a handle by a chain.

name: Fork / Trident
description: A spear with a double or triple-pronged head, can be used to entangle.

name: Frying Pan
description: A cooking tool that can be used as an improvised weapon.

name: Gauntlet/Pommel
description: An unarmed attack using a gauntlet or the pommel of a weapon

name: Great Axe
description: A larger, heavier axe for combat

name: Great Flail
description: A larger, two-handed version of a flail.

name: Greatclub
description: A heavy, two-handed club.

name: Hand Axe
description: Small, light axe, good for throwing

name: Hand Crossbow
description: A small, one-handed crossbow with short range and less power.

name: Heavy Crossbow
description: A more powerful crossbow with longer range and more damage.

name: Hook
description: A hook-shaped weapon or implement.

name: Javelin
description: A spear-like weapon designed for throwing.

name: Kick
description: An unarmed attack

name: Lance
description: A larger, sturdier spear, best used when mounted.

name: Light Crossbow
description: A lighter crossbow with shorter range and less damage.

name: Light Mace
description: A small, light mace, better suited for mounted combat or smaller characters.

name: Longbow
description: A bow with a longer stave for more power and range.

name: Longsword / Scimitar
description: A versatile, medium-length sword for slashing and thrusting.

name: Mace
description: A standard bludgeoning weapon with a head.

name: Mattock (Footman's Pick)
description: A larger pickaxe, similar to the military pick, but larger and heavier.

name: Maul / Great Mace
description: Larger, two-handed versions of the hammer and mace.

name: Morningstar
description: A mace with spikes or blades on the head.

name: Net
description: A weapon used to entangle.

name: Pickaxe (Military Pick)
description: A weapon with a sharpened spike instead of a blade.

name: Pitchfork
description: A tool that can be used as an improvised weapon.

name: Pole Arm
description: A long pole weapon, typically with a blade, axe, or spike on top.

name: Punch
description: An unarmed attack

name: Quarterstaff
description: A long pole that functions as a headless spear.

name: Sap/Blackjack
description: A small, subduing weapon.

name: Scythe
description: A large, inward-curved cutting weapon

name: Shortbow
description: A bow with a shorter stave, good for smaller characters.

name: Shortsword / Cutlass
description: A shorter sword, good for thrusting or slashing.

name: Sickle
description: An inward-curved cutting weapon

name: Silver Arrow, Longbow
description: An arrow composed of arrowhead, shaft, and flights. The arrowhead is made of silver.

name: Silver Arrow, Shortbow
description: An arrow composed of arrowhead, shaft, and flights. The arrowhead is made of silver.

name: Silver Dagger
description: A dagger with a silver blade, effective against lycanthropes.

name: Silver Walking Stick/Staff
description: A walking stick with a silver head or handle.

name: Sling
description: A simple tool that launches a small projectile at high speed.
oneLiner: Sling, 1gp, Dmg 1d4 with sling bullets, 1d3 with stones, *lb

name: Spade
description: A tool that can be used as an improvised weapon.

name: Spear
description: A simple weapon with a pointed end. Can be thrown one-handed, used in melee one-handed, or melee two-handed.

name: Torch (fire damage)
description: A source of light that can be used as an improvised weapon, dealing fire damage.

name: Two-Handed Sword
description: A large sword requiring two hands to use.

name: Warhammer
description: A hammer balanced for throwing or melee.

name: Whip
description: A flexible weapon good for entangling.

name: Brass
description: Brass, per lb. Price: 1sp/lb.

name: Bronze
description: Bronze, per lb. Price: 7cp/lb.

name: Copper
description: Copper, per lb. Price: 9cp/lb.

name: Electrum
description: Electrum, per lb. Price: 9ep/lb.

name: Gold
description: Gold, per lb. Price: 9gp/lb.

name: Iron
description: Iron, per lb. Price: 1sp/lb.

name: Lead
description: Lead, per lb. Price: 4cp/lb.

name: Mithral
description: Mithral, per lb. Price: 40gp/lb.

name: Platinum
description: Platinum, per lb. Price: 9pp/lb.

name: Silver
description: Silver, per lb. Price: 9sp/lb.

name: Steel
description: Steel, per lb. Price: 3sp/lb.

name: Tin
description: Tin, per lb. Price: 2sp/lb.

name: Zinc
description: Zinc, per lb. Price: 8sp/lb.

name: Rod of Cancellation
description: This rod may only be successfully used once. If struck against another magic item, it utterly destroys all enchantments within the item; this expends the rod's magic. A roll to hit is required if the target item is held by another character or creature.
oneLiner: Rod of Cancellation: destroys all enchantments in a touched magic item (single use)

name: Snake Staff
description: A walking staff +1. When used by a Cleric, the user may command the staff to transform into a constrictor snake on a successful hit. The snake wraps around a target up to man-sized and holds them fast for 1d4 turns (save vs. Spells negates). The snake has AC 15, MV 20', and 20 HP; damage heals when it returns to staff form. If killed in snake form, the magic is destroyed. No charges — usable any number of times per day.
oneLiner: Snake Staff: +1 walking staff; Cleric can transform it into a constricting snake on hit (no charges)

name: Staff of Commanding
description: This staff can cast charm person and charm monster spells, and can grant a power equivalent to a Potion of Plant Control. Each function uses one charge. A newly created staff has 30 charges; one found in a hoard has 3d10 charges remaining. Spell effects operate at 8th level.
oneLiner: Staff of Commanding: charm person, charm monster, plant control (1 charge each; 3d10 charges)

name: Staff of Healing
description: This staff can heal 1d6+1 hit points per charge expended, as the spell cure light wounds. Alternately, with an expenditure of two charges, the staff can cast cure disease. This staff is only usable by a Cleric. A newly created staff has 30 charges; one found in a hoard has 3d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Staff of Healing: heals 1d6+1 HP (1 charge) or cure disease (2 charges); Clerics only (3d10 charges)

name: Staff of Power
description: This staff has the following powers at 1 charge each: lightning bolt (6d6), fireball (6d6), cone of cold (6d6), continual light, and telekinesis (1d6 turns). The staff is also a walking staff +2 and functions as a Staff of Striking. It can be used for a retributive strike — when broken, all remaining charges release in a 30' radius dealing 1d6 damage per charge (save vs. Spells for half). A newly created staff has 30 charges; one found in a hoard has 3d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Staff of Power: lightning bolt/fireball/cone of cold (6d6 each), continual light, telekinesis (+2 staff; 3d10 charges)

name: Staff of Striking
description: Treated as a +1 weapon for purposes of what it can hit. When wielded by a Cleric, a command word causes a striking effect: 1 charge adds 1d6 damage to the next strike, 2 charges add 2d6, and 3 charges add 3d6. If not used after the command word is spoken, the effect dissipates after one turn. A newly created staff has 30 charges; one found in a hoard has 3d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Staff of Striking: +1 to hit; Cleric adds 1–3d6 damage per charge (3d10 charges)

name: Staff of Wizardry
description: Equivalent to the Staff of Power, with additional powers: invisibility, passwall, web, and conjure elementals (conjures staff elementals). Each power costs one charge. The staff is also a walking staff +2. A newly created staff has 30 charges; one found in a hoard has 3d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Staff of Wizardry: Staff of Power + invisibility, passwall, web, conjure elementals (+2 staff; 3d10 charges)

name: Wand of Cold
description: Generates a conical blast of cold doing 6d8 damage (save vs. Magic Wands for half). The cone spreads from the tip of the wand to a width of 30' at a distance of 40' away. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Cold: 6d8 cold damage in a 40' cone (save for half; 2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Enemy Detection
description: Makes all enemies of the user within 60' glow with a greenish-white light for one round. Even hidden or invisible enemies glow, revealing them. Enemies completely out of sight (e.g., behind a wall) cannot be seen. All undead and animated constructs within range also glow regardless of intent. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Enemy Detection: enemies within 60' glow for 1 round (reveals invisible; 2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Fear
description: Generates the effect of the spell cause fear (the reverse of remove fear). A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Fear: causes fear as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Fireballs
description: Generates fireballs exactly as the spell, dealing 6d6 damage. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Fireballs: 6d6 fireball as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Illusion
description: Allows the user to create illusions equivalent to the spell phantasmal force. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Illusion: phantasmal force as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Lightning Bolts
description: Generates lightning bolts exactly as the spell, dealing 6d6 damage. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Lightning Bolts: 6d6 lightning bolt as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Magic Detection
description: Grants the user a power equivalent to the spell detect magic. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Magic Detection: detect magic as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Paralysis
description: Creates the effect of the spell hold person. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Paralysis: hold person as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Polymorph
description: Can be used to cast either polymorph self or polymorph other. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Polymorph: polymorph self or other (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Secret Door Detection
description: Grants the user a power similar to the spell find traps, but which reveals secret doors rather than traps. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Secret Door Detection: reveals secret doors (2d10 charges)

name: Wand of Trap Detection
description: Grants the user a power equivalent to the spell find traps. A newly created wand has 20 charges; one found in a hoard has 2d10 charges remaining.
oneLiner: Wand of Trap Detection: find traps as the spell (2d10 charges)

name: Item of Blasting
description: When this device is played or activated (form is typically a horn or instrument), it creates a powerful blast of sound filling a cone 10' long and 2' wide at the base. Those within the area suffer 2d6 damage and are deafened for 1 full turn (save vs. Death Ray for half damage and 1 round deafness). Double damage against buildings and fortifications.
oneLiner: Item of Blasting (Horn/Instrument): 2d6 sonic cone, deafens 1 turn

name: Item of Blending
description: The wearer of this item (typically a cloak or ring) becomes nearly invisible, granting an 80% chance to move about unnoticed. If detected, the wearer can still be attacked without significant penalty.
oneLiner: Item of Blending (Cloak/Ring): 80% chance to move unnoticed

name: Item of Cold Resistance
description: The wearer receives protection as the spell resist cold, but the protection works continually.
oneLiner: Item of Cold Resistance (Cloak/Ring): continuous resist cold

name: Item of Comprehension
description: The wearer (typically a headband, hat, or tiara) can read any language, including magical script. Magic-users gain the constant effect of read magic. Non-magical text reading follows the limitations of the read languages spell.
oneLiner: Item of Comprehension (Headband/Hat): read any language; magic-users gain read magic

name: Item of Control Animal
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can charm up to 6 HD of animals within 60', similar to charm person but only affecting animals (including giant animals, excluding fantastic creatures and anything smarter than a dog or cat). The wearer may end control at will to free hit dice for new targets.
oneLiner: Item of Control Animal (Ring): charm up to 6 HD of animals within 60'

name: Item of Control Human
description: The wearer (typically a ring) may cast charm person at will at any target within 60', once per round. The wearer cannot control more than 6 HD or levels of humanoids at a time, but may release controlled creatures to free capacity for new targets.
oneLiner: Item of Control Human (Ring): charm person at will, up to 6 HD of humanoids

name: Item of Control Plant
description: The wearer (typically a ring) may create an effect equivalent to a Potion of Plant Control at will, affecting plants or plant creatures within 60'. The effect lasts as long as the wearer remains within range. A saving throw is allowed as for the potion.
oneLiner: Item of Control Plant (Ring): Potion of Plant Control effect at will within 60'

name: Item of Courage
description: When this device is played or activated (form is typically a horn, drums, or instrument), all friendly characters and creatures within 60' are affected as by the spell remove fear.
oneLiner: Item of Courage (Horn/Instrument): remove fear for all allies within 60'

name: Item of Deception
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) gains the power of the Deceiver: attackers believe the wearer is 3 feet from their true location. The attacker's first strike always misses, and thereafter the attacker suffers -2 on all attack rolls. Does not affect mindless creatures, constructs, or undead.
oneLiner: Item of Deception (Cloak/Ring): first attack always misses; -2 to all subsequent attacks

name: Item of Delusion
description: Cursed item. The wearer believes this is some other useful magical device and behaves accordingly (e.g., believing themselves invisible). Unlike a Potion of Delusion, this effect is not dispelled by damage — only remove curse can free the wearer.
oneLiner: Item of Delusion (cursed): wearer believes it is another magic item; only remove curse breaks it

name: Item of Djinni Summoning
description: Each device of this type has a specific djinni bound to it. Rubbing the device while wearing it summons the djinni, who appears the next round and serves the wearer for up to 1 hour per day (summoned at most once per day). If the bound djinni is ever slain, the device loses all magical properties.
oneLiner: Item of Djinni Summoning (Ring): summons a bound djinni; up to 1 hour/day service

name: Item of Doom
description: Cursed item. When this device is played or activated (typically a horn or instrument), it creates an effect of despair and doom on those who hear it, causing fear or worse effects at the GM's discretion.
oneLiner: Item of Doom (Horn/Instrument, cursed): causes despair and fear in those who hear it

name: Item of Fire Resistance
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) receives protection as the spell resist fire, but the protection works continually.
oneLiner: Item of Fire Resistance (Cloak/Ring): continuous resist fire

name: Item of Invisibility
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) becomes invisible as the spell invisibility. Most such items provide invisibility continuously while worn, but attacking or casting a spell may end the effect.
oneLiner: Item of Invisibility (Cloak/Ring): continuous invisibility; ends on attack or spell

name: Item of Levitation
description: The wearer (typically boots or a belt) can levitate as the spell, rising or descending at will. The item allows vertical movement only; horizontal movement is achieved by pushing off surfaces.
oneLiner: Item of Levitation (Boots/Belt): levitate at will (vertical movement only)

name: Item of Mind Reading
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can read the surface thoughts of any creature within 60' as the spell ESP. Creatures of 0 intelligence or those protected by magic cannot be read.
oneLiner: Item of Mind Reading (Ring): ESP as the spell, within 60'

name: Item of Panic
description: Cursed item. When this device is played or activated (typically a horn or instrument), it causes panic and rout in all friendly creatures within range rather than aiding the user.
oneLiner: Item of Panic (Horn/Instrument, cursed): causes friendly forces to flee

name: Item of Penetrating Vision
description: The wearer (typically a lens, spectacles, or goggles) can see through solid objects and materials as the spell x-ray vision, revealing hidden doors, creatures, and objects concealed by walls or floors.
oneLiner: Item of Penetrating Vision (Goggles/Lens): see through solid objects as x-ray vision

name: Item of Protection +1
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class and all saving throws. Only the most powerful protection item worn functions; wearing two items with the same bonus does not stack.
oneLiner: Item of Protection +1 (Cloak/Ring): +1 AC and saving throws

name: Item of Protection +2
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class and all saving throws. Only the most powerful protection item worn functions.
oneLiner: Item of Protection +2 (Cloak/Ring): +2 AC and saving throws

name: Item of Protection +3
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) gains a +3 bonus to Armor Class and all saving throws. Only the most powerful protection item worn functions.
oneLiner: Item of Protection +3 (Cloak/Ring): +3 AC and saving throws

name: Item of Protection from Energy Drain
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) is protected from the energy drain attacks of undead creatures. Any energy drain attempt made against the wearer fails automatically.
oneLiner: Item of Protection from Energy Drain (Cloak/Ring): immune to undead energy drain

name: Item of Protection from Scrying
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) cannot be detected or observed by magical scrying of any kind, including crystal balls, ESP, and clairvoyance spells.
oneLiner: Item of Protection from Scrying (Cloak/Ring): immune to magical detection and scrying

name: Item of Regeneration
description: The wearer (typically a ring) regenerates 1 hit point per turn. Lost limbs regrow over a period of days. Fire and acid damage cannot be regenerated. The wearer cannot die from most wounds so long as the item is worn, though sufficiently catastrophic damage (such as beheading) may still kill.
oneLiner: Item of Regeneration (Ring): regenerate 1 HP/turn; regrow lost limbs

name: Item of Scrying
description: This device (typically a crystal ball or bowl) allows the user to observe distant persons or places as the spell clairvoyance. The user must concentrate and can view the location for up to 1 hour per use.
oneLiner: Item of Scrying (Crystal Ball/Bowl): view distant locations as clairvoyance

name: Item of Scrying, Superior
description: As a standard scrying device, but additionally allows the user to hear sounds at the viewed location (as clairaudience) and to communicate mentally with observed creatures.
oneLiner: Item of Scrying, Superior (Crystal Ball): scrying + clairaudience + mental communication

name: Item of Speed
description: The wearer (typically boots or a belt) moves at double normal speed and gains one extra attack per round in melee combat.
oneLiner: Item of Speed (Boots/Belt): double movement, +1 attack per round

name: Item of Spell Storing
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can have spells stored within the device by a spellcaster. The stored spells can be released by the wearer at will, even if the wearer is not a spellcaster. The number of spells that can be stored varies.
oneLiner: Item of Spell Storing (Ring): stores spells that anyone can release at will

name: Item of Spell Turning
description: The wearer (typically a cloak or ring) has a chance to reflect spells cast directly at them back upon the caster. Area-of-effect spells and spells not targeted at the wearer are not affected.
oneLiner: Item of Spell Turning (Cloak/Ring): reflects targeted spells back at the caster

name: Item of Stealth
description: The wearer (typically boots or a belt) moves in complete silence, automatically succeeding at any move silently checks and leaving no audible trace of passage.
oneLiner: Item of Stealth (Boots/Belt): move in complete silence

name: Item of Telekinesis
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can move objects at a distance of up to 120' by mental force, as the spell telekinesis. The item can move up to 200 lbs.
oneLiner: Item of Telekinesis (Ring): move objects up to 200 lbs within 120' by thought

name: Item of Telepathy
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can communicate mind-to-mind with any creature within 60' that the wearer can see, regardless of language barriers.
oneLiner: Item of Telepathy (Ring): mental communication within 60', no language barrier

name: Item of Teleportation
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can teleport at will as the spell, once per day. The wearer must have seen or studied the destination to teleport safely.
oneLiner: Item of Teleportation (Ring): teleport at will once per day

name: Item of True Seeing
description: The wearer (typically goggles or a lens) can see invisible creatures, illusions, and the true form of shapeshifted or polymorphed creatures, as the spell true seeing.
oneLiner: Item of True Seeing (Goggles/Lens): see invisible, see through illusions and shapeshifting

name: Item of Water Walking
description: The wearer (typically boots or a belt) can walk on water and other liquid surfaces as if they were solid ground.
oneLiner: Item of Water Walking (Boots/Belt): walk on liquid surfaces

name: Item of Weakness
description: Cursed item. The wearer (typically a ring or girdle) suffers a reduction in Strength to 3, causing a -3 penalty to attack rolls and damage. The curse is not revealed until the item is first worn. Only remove curse can allow the item to be removed.
oneLiner: Item of Weakness (Ring/Girdle, cursed): reduces Strength to 3; only remove curse frees wearer

name: Item of Wishes
description: The wearer (typically a ring) can make wishes as the spell wish, one per charge. Wishes are powerful but literal — the GM interprets results carefully. Items with this power typically have only 1d4 wishes remaining when found.
oneLiner: Item of Wishes (Ring): grant wishes as the spell (typically 1d4 remaining)

name: Bag of Devouring
description: Cursed item. This bag appears identical to a Bag of Holding, but it actually leads to the gullet of an extra-dimensional creature. Any item placed inside vanishes forever. Any creature that places a hand or limb inside suffers 1d4 damage per round until they pull free; a creature fully entering the bag is consumed and killed.
oneLiner: Bag of Devouring (cursed): looks like Bag of Holding; devours everything placed inside

name: Bag of Holding
description: This magical bag can hold up to 10,000 coins of weight regardless of its outward size (which appears to be a normal sack). The bag itself weighs very little when empty. Items placed inside are effectively weightless while stored.
oneLiner: Bag of Holding: holds 10,000 cn regardless of size; contents are weightless

name: Boots of Traveling and Leaping
description: These magical boots double the wearer's normal movement rate and allow prodigious leaps — up to 10' high and 30' horizontally. The wearer never tires from walking or running.
oneLiner: Boots of Traveling and Leaping: double movement, leap 10' up/30' across, never tire

name: Broom of Flying
description: This enchanted broom can carry one rider through the air at a movement rate of 40' per round (or 20' with two riders). The broom can be commanded by its rider to fly to a known location on its own.
oneLiner: Broom of Flying: fly at MV 40' (20' with 2 riders); can fly independently to known locations

name: Device of Summoning Elementals
description: This device can summon and bind an elemental of a specific type (determined when the device is found). The elemental serves the summoner for up to 1 hour. The device can be used once per day. The elemental summoned has the standard statistics for its type.
oneLiner: Device of Summoning Elementals: summons and binds a specific elemental type once/day

name: Efreeti Bottle
description: This ornate bottle contains an efreeti bound to serve the opener. The efreeti serves for up to 1,001 days before being released. It can grant up to 3 wishes before being freed (or if the 1,001 days expire). If freed early or mistreated, the efreeti may turn hostile.
oneLiner: Efreeti Bottle: efreeti serves for 1,001 days or until 3 wishes granted

name: Flying Carpet
description: This magical carpet can carry up to three passengers and flies at a movement rate of 30' per round (or 40' with one passenger, 35' with two). The carpet is controlled by mental command from the lead rider.
oneLiner: Flying Carpet: fly at MV 40'/35'/30' for 1/2/3 passengers; mental control

name: Gauntlets of Ogre Power
description: These iron gauntlets grant the wearer the Strength of an ogre (equivalent to Strength 18+3), providing +3 to attack rolls and damage, and allowing the wearer to carry loads as if they were an ogre.
oneLiner: Gauntlets of Ogre Power: Strength as an ogre (+3 to hit and damage)

name: Girdle of Giant Strength
description: This magical girdle grants the wearer the Strength of a hill giant, providing a significant bonus to attack rolls and damage (typically +4 or as determined by the GM). The wearer can also throw boulders as a giant.
oneLiner: Girdle of Giant Strength: Strength of a hill giant, throw boulders

name: Mirror of Imprisonment
description: Any creature that sees its reflection in this mirror must save vs. Spells or be drawn into the mirror and imprisoned within. Up to 20 creatures can be held within the mirror at once. Imprisoned creatures do not age or need food. They can be freed by breaking the mirror or by a wish.
oneLiner: Mirror of Imprisonment: creatures that see reflection save or are trapped within (holds up to 20)

name: Rope of Climbing
description: This 50-foot rope can climb, knot, unknot, or coil itself on command. It can fasten itself to any anchor and support up to 3,000 coins of weight. When commanded, it moves at 10' per round and can be directed to tie or untie itself.
oneLiner: Rope of Climbing: 50' rope climbs and ties itself on command; holds 3,000 cn
